summary:
We developed a web-based Astronaut Health Monitoring and Guidance System designed to support astronauts during long-duration space missions. The platform allows astronauts to record daily and routine health check-ins, monitor vital health indicators, visualize health trends, and access personalized health recommendations.

The system evaluates numerical and rating-based health parameters using a rule-based assessment engine that identifies deviations from acceptable ranges and provides appropriate guidance. It also includes a centralized health dashboard, health history and reports, a human body map, mission configuration, and medical support features.

Our solution addresses the NASA Space Apps Challenge by helping astronauts monitor potential health changes associated with spaceflight hazards, including radiation, isolation, altered gravity, and confined environments. By making health information easier to understand and act upon, the platform supports early awareness, informed decision-making, and proactive health management.

This is important because maintaining astronaut health is essential for mission safety, performance, and the success of future long-duration human space exploration.
details:
1. What does the project do, and how does it work?

AstraVita is a web-based astronaut health monitoring and guidance platform designed to support astronauts during long-duration space missions. It provides a centralized interface where astronauts can record their health information through daily check-ins and routine assessments.

The platform monitors important health indicators, including blood pressure, heart rate, blood glucose, body temperature, sleep duration, and mood. It organizes the submitted information, presents health trends and historical reports, and identifies values that may require attention.

A rule-based assessment engine evaluates recorded health indicators against predefined reference ranges and generates corresponding recommendations. Astronauts can also explore health information through features such as a health dashboard, human body map, recommendations page, mission configuration, and medical support section.

2. What benefits does it have?

  • Continuous health awareness: Helps astronauts monitor changes in their health over time.
  • Early identification of concerns: Highlights unusual readings and potential health-related concerns.
  • Personalized guidance: Provides recommendations based on recorded health indicators.
  • Centralized information: Keeps check-ins, trends, reports, and recommendations organized in one platform.
  • Better decision support: Makes health information easier to understand and review during missions.
  • Accessible interface: Presents complex health information through a structured and visual dashboard.

3. What is the intended impact of the project?

The primary goal of AstraVita is to improve astronaut health awareness and support proactive health management during long-duration space missions.

Space missions expose astronauts to several challenges, including space radiation, isolation and confinement, altered gravity, distance from Earth, and closed environments. These conditions can affect physical and psychological well-being.

AstraVita aims to help astronauts recognize changes in their health, understand potential concerns, and access relevant guidance without depending entirely on continuous direct communication with Earth-based medical teams.

Ultimately, the project seeks to contribute to safer, more informed, and more sustainable human space exploration.

4. What tools, programming languages, and software were used?

The project was developed using web development technologies and a database-driven backend.

  • HTML5: Structure of the web pages.
  • CSS3: Page styling, layouts, and responsive interface design.
  • JavaScript: Frontend interactions, form handling, dynamic content, and API communication.
  • Node.js: Backend runtime environment.
  • Express.js: Backend server and API development.
  • MongoDB: Storage of astronaut profiles, health records, check-ins, and related information.
  • Mongoose: Database models and interaction with MongoDB.
  • REST APIs: Communication between the frontend and backend.
  • Visual Studio Code: Development environment.

The system uses a rule-based assessment approach to interpret health indicators and generate recommendations. It does not depend on training a large machine learning model.

5. How is the project creative?

AstraVita combines multiple health-monitoring functions into one astronaut-focused platform rather than treating each health indicator as an isolated measurement.

Its creative aspects include:

  • A unified dashboard for monitoring different aspects of astronaut health.
  • Separate daily and routine check-ins to organize health data collection.
  • A recommendation engine that translates recorded values into understandable guidance.
  • Visual health trends and historical reports to help identify changes over time.
  • A human body map to make health information more intuitive.
  • Mission-specific configuration to accommodate the requirements of different space missions.

The project emphasizes practical usability and understandable health information rather than simply collecting large amounts of data.

6. What factors did the team consider?

During development, the team considered several factors:

  • Spaceflight conditions: The effects of radiation, isolation, altered gravity, distance from Earth, and closed environments.
  • Relevant health indicators: Selecting measurable parameters that can provide useful information about astronaut well-being.
  • Usability: Designing an interface that astronauts can navigate efficiently during demanding missions.
  • Data organization: Structuring daily and routine health records for easier monitoring and analysis.
  • Recommendation clarity: Making system-generated guidance understandable and actionable.
  • Scalability: Developing a modular architecture that can accommodate additional indicators and features.
  • Reliability: Maintaining organized data handling and communication between the frontend, backend, and database.
  • Limitations: Recognizing that automated recommendations are decision-support information, not a replacement for professional medical diagnosis or treatment.

Astra: Beyond Earth. Within Health.
